dedupe_keys.name: bytreatlas trekrone project urban tree crown maps and ecosystem service values for oslo bærum kristiansand and bodø

description: The urban tree atlas is an ArcGIS Online application showing the map results of the Trekrone project, led by the Norwegian Institute for Nature Research, which maps and values urban trees in the building zones of Bodø, Bærum, Kristiansand and Oslo. The Oslo atlas read on 2026-09-28 has a map tab with tree crown data, the physical regulating effects of ecosystem services, crown visibility and a layer of local ground temperature regulation for the hottest summer on record (2018 for Oslo, Bærum and Kristiansand, 2023 for Bodø) against a no-tree scenario, and a tab of trees in the municipal tree register with species, trunk diameter, height, crown area and computed physical and economic ecosystem service values, exportable to Excel. Methods and code are documented on GitHub and results in NINA report 2337. Access is free in the viewer; the app states no licence. Caveats: crown mapping covers only the building zone, and the ecosystem values are model estimates. It supports heat adaptation studies, such as locating streets where losing canopy would raise ground temperatures. Related record: the Helsinki metropolitan tree canopy atlas offers a comparable Nordic layer.
